newsitem.title: UK: North Sea crude rises on refining margins.
newsitem.headline: North Sea crude rises on refining margins.

text.p: Wet North Sea crude rallied on Tuesday and traders said the rise was mainly due to good refining margins while paper Brent was bolstered by export problems in Nigeria.

June Brent was up 22 cents at $18.56 by 1352 GMT, after reaching a high of $18.64 in earlier trade, pushed up on Shell Nigeria's declaration of a force majeure on exports from its Nigerian Bonny terminal because of a contractors' strike there.
"Firming, that's how we see them," one refiner said of North Sea grades. "I guess the reason for that is good refining margins and the contango."
Cheaper prompt oil often encourages buying to build up stocks.
But he warned that the rally would be short-lived and "it would fizzle out as soon as the contango bottoms out".
Brent CFDs and spreads also firmed.
CFDs rose with next week's dates talked in the June Brent - 36 cents/-33 cents range while May 5-9 was quoted at -35/-32 cents and May 12-16 at -33/-30 cents.
May/June tightened sharply to -15/-12 cents from Monday's -20/-17 cents while June/July was set at -6/-4 cents compared with -12/-10 cents a day earlier.
Two CFDs traded, an April 22-25 was done at June Brent -42 cents, and an April 28-09 changed hands at June -35 cents and two June/July intermonth spreads were traded at -7 cents.
A May/June Brent was heard traded at -16 cents.
Traders said no physical trades took place early. Two Brent cargoes were due to pass down the paper chains on Tuesday.

Refiners said a a lot of crude was moving out of the region, "the primary reason for that is that you got a lot of refining capacity coming back in the U.S. and Europe". Shipping sources said two North Sea crude shipments for early May lifting were heading to the U.S. Gulf.

In the Mediterranean, negotiations between Syria's state oil company Sytrol and term lifters continue over the May prices and traders said the issue would be settled soon. One trader said that the Syrians claimed that one term lifter had accepted its asking price of Dated Brent -82 cents for Syrian Light for May, but other lifters were still hoping for a small discount. --Haitham Haddadin, London newsroom +44 171 542 8145
